timeline.title: A Short History of Going Away
items: Marco Polo set out from Venice for Asia. He did not get home for about 24 years. Some holiday.
Young travellers crossed Europe for months, chasing art, music, ruins and sunshine.
Thomas Cook took hundreds of people on a day trip by train, and the group holiday was born.
The first Boeing 747 passenger flight took off, and flying abroad began to open up for millions.
today: {days} days in {place}. Not in the history books yet, but the best trip ever taken, if you ask us.

letters.title: What the World Has Said About Travel
items: Not all those who wander are lost.
J. R. R. Tolkien, The Fellowship of the Ring
A journey is best measured in friends, rather than miles.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
A good companion shortens the longest road.
letters.hand: They all say it beautifully. We just say: where to next?

facts.title: The Science of Adventure
items: New places light up the brain's reward system, the same one that makes good news feel so good.
Studies suggest just looking forward to a trip can make people happier for weeks before they go.
Research shows experiences bring longer lasting happiness than things. Memories never go out of style.
A breathtaking view sparks awe, which studies link to feeling kinder and more connected.
The first powered aeroplane flight, in 1903, lasted just 12 seconds.
After a long flight, the body clock catches up at roughly one time zone a day.
facts.hand: Science can explain a lot. It cannot explain why holiday food always tastes better.

world.lead: Because you went, the world got:
items: A few more strangers who smiled back.
A café that will remember your order.
More footprints on a beach somewhere.
A sunset that finally had the right audience.
A thousand new photos, mostly of food.
Proof that getting lost is the best part.
And a story you will be telling for years.

note.title: What we believe a journey is
paras: We make magazines for a living, and some of them make us want to pack a bag. This was one of them.
We believe the best part of any trip is not the place. It is the person beside you on the bus, the shared plate, the wrong turn that becomes the story you tell for the rest of your lives.
{who}, someone wanted to keep this trip safe. Not in a phone full of photos, but here, in pages you can hold: the views, the meals, the moments only you share.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, the best adventures are still ahead of you.
note.wish: Wherever you go next, go together. Bon voyage, always.
